paragraphs: A thunderstorm had moved into a coffee cup on the table. Yellow Duck Sweater sat on the saucer and waited, because no new runs had come in and waiting was the one event nobody had trained it for. The cup was as wide as an arena. Its rim ran in a perfect ring, and the coffee below was black as a pit, only this pit had weather. A grey cloud rolled across it like a cat turning around before sleep. Each flash of lightning showed a teaspoon lying across the cup like a bridge nobody had asked for.

The duck did not want to walk the spoon. It walked the spoon anyway, one careful foot and then the other, counting steps the way it counted iterations, and halfway across it found the storm was only the size of a pillow. Rain fell in single warm drops, each landing on the knitted duckling on its sweater with a pat, as if checking that it was real. The duck said wheee, very quietly, in case the thunder was listening. Then the cloud curled up at the far end of the spoon, and a rainbow no wider than a thread rose from the coffee and hooked itself over the rim.

The cup was as wide as an arena. Its rim ran in a perfect ring, and the coffee below was black as a pit, only this pit had weather. A grey cloud rolled across it like a cat turning around before sleep. Each flash of lightning showed a teaspoon lying across the cup like a bridge nobody had asked for.

The duck did not want to walk the spoon. It walked the spoon anyway, one careful foot and then the other, counting steps the way it counted iterations, and halfway across it found the storm was only the size of a pillow. Rain fell in single warm drops, each landing on the knitted duckling on its sweater with a pat, as if checking that it was real. The duck said wheee, very quietly, in case the thunder was listening. Then the cloud curled up at the far end of the spoon, and a rainbow no wider than a thread rose from the coffee and hooked itself over the rim.
imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The robot duck in its yellow duckling sweater sits alone on a saucer as wide as a skating rink beside a giant coffee cup on a wooden table, head tilted toward the cup's rim. Panel 2: Looking down into the cup from the rim: the coffee is a dark round pit, and a small grey storm cloud rolls across it with tiny lightning flashing, the circular rim a ring around everything. Panel 3: Close-up: the duck's round camera eye is wide, with little flashes of lightning reflected in the lens and steam curling past its head. Panel 4: The duck walks along a silver teaspoon laid across the cup like a narrow bridge over the stormy coffee, one orange foot placed carefully ahead of the other. Panel 5: Halfway across the spoon, a pillow-sized grey cloud drifts up beside the duck and drops single raindrops that land on the knitted duckling on its sweater. Panel 6: The duck sits at the far end of the spoon with the little cloud curled up asleep beside it, while a thin rainbow rises from the coffee and hooks over the cup's rim. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
